boss_summary: The selected V3 boundary honestly separates pure policy, sealed Windows measurement, a future wrapper-owned live lease, and an external owner capability. It directionally closes every V2 bypass class: production injection is forbidden; expectations are freeze-derived; raw evidence and dependencies are bound; target identity is parent-handle and leaf derived; process blockers are policy-derived; chronology and current/parent identity are explicit; and real-Windows evidence is separated from fixture and static evidence. The documents also consistently deny implementation, execution, human-identity, publication, durability, set-atomicity, and writer-exclusion claims. However, the current design is not closed enough to implement without interpretation. Its launcher/freeze/review hash topology can become circular, execution-freeze timing ambiguously mixes stable pre-restart identities with ephemeral post-restart process identities, the journal/lease terminal ordering permits an unclear post-completed drift state, Windows process liveness is described with incorrect signaling terminology, hardlink policy is not closed, and the test suite's zero-delta requirement conflicts with its synthetic replacement case unless scoped. These are blocking design errata, not evidence that any implementation has failed or passed.

v2_design_failure_adjudication.v2_failure: production provider, clock, parent, path, label, process, or authorization injection
v2_design_failure_adjudication.basis: The sealed production surface forbids those parameters, isolates test entry points and schemas, requires actual Windows provenance, and adds static closure tests.

v2_design_failure_adjudication.v2_failure: local JSON impersonating Lowell, checker, or boss authority
v2_design_failure_adjudication.basis: Pure policy may only scope-check a projection and must report human identity and origin unverified; a non-model-forgeable product/runtime capability remains outside repository code.

v2_design_failure_adjudication.v2_failure: lossy raw bridge and dynamically unpinned V1 or policy dependencies
v2_design_failure_adjudication.basis: The complete raw record and detached digest are retained, and every runtime dependency must be verified before import.

v2_design_failure_adjudication.v2_failure: parent swap, parent alias, or logical-token to different same-parent file
v2_design_failure_adjudication.basis: Roles, normalized tokens, parents, and leaves are allowlist-derived under retained root and parent handles; parent and child identities are bound and aliases are rejected.

v2_design_failure_adjudication.v2_failure: caller-supplied contradictory process subsets and incomplete current/parent continuity
v2_design_failure_adjudication.basis: One raw PID/start/executable identity set feeds deterministic policy-derived subsets; exact current and direct ancestry identities must remain continuous across prepare and publish.

v2_design_failure_adjudication.v2_failure: boot chronology, Windows, NTFS, volume-root, and observation ordering gaps
v2_design_failure_adjudication.basis: The contract explicitly orders freeze, boot, capture, observations, validation, and dual monotonic clocks while binding OS, architecture, volume and root identities.

v2_design_failure_adjudication.v2_failure: caller-resubmitted prepare evidence and JSON-only lease replay
v2_design_failure_adjudication.basis: Prepare digests must be retained independently and publish requires the same nonserializable in-process lease and owner capability.

v2_design_failure_adjudication.v2_failure: fake-only tests misrepresented as actual Windows evidence
v2_design_failure_adjudication.basis: Fixture, real-Windows temporary-root, production-closure, and canonical-execution evidence classes are separated and non-interchangeable.

blocking_design_errata.title: Launcher, component lock, execution freeze, and review hashes lack one unambiguous acyclic trust topology
blocking_design_errata.evidence: The policy docket says the generic wrapper does not hard-code its own or the future freeze digest and a trusted launcher supplies detached digests. The Windows docket says the sealed launcher reads an expected V3 freeze SHA from a launcher constant before import. The component lock itself includes the launcher and wrapper hashes plus independent evidence hashes, while later review artifacts are also expected to pin the component lock or freeze.
blocking_design_errata.risk: Hard-coding the digest of an object that contains the launcher's hash creates a self-cycle. Including checker, premortem, or boss artifacts that themselves bind the same component lock creates an indirect review cycle. An implementer could silently choose a weaker trust anchor.
blocking_design_errata.required_resolution: Publish one explicit directed acyclic artifact graph. At minimum: code-and-test lock without its own digest or reviews; detached code-lock digest supplied by a product/runtime trust root outside that lock; reviews that bind the code-lock digest; a separate reviewed release record that binds code-lock plus review hashes; execution freeze that binds the detached reviewed release digest; and runtime capability that supplies the independently trusted execution-freeze digest. No artifact may contain the hash of an artifact that directly or transitively hashes it. State exactly which external product/runtime primitive is the first trust anchor.

blocking_design_errata.title: Execution-freeze timing ambiguously mixes stable pre-restart identity with ephemeral post-restart process identity
blocking_design_errata.evidence: The design resolution says execution freeze is created after separately authorized pre-restart identity capture and binds exact file, root, process, environment identities and the pre-freeze boot. The policy docket's execution-freeze rows bind stable file and parent identities and process-policy data, while live current and parent PID/start identities are supposed to be measured after restart.
blocking_design_errata.risk: A literal implementation could freeze a pre-restart PID/start token and make every valid post-restart run impossible, or omit required stable executable identities by calling all process identity post-restart.
blocking_design_errata.required_resolution: Split identity classes explicitly. Before restart, freeze only stable code, allowlist, file/root/volume identities, permitted executable file identities and hashes, process classification policy, environment allowlist, and pre-freeze boot identity. Never freeze ephemeral live PID, process start token, handle value, lease nonce, or live ancestry as a post-restart expectation. Measure those after restart and bind only their prepare-to-publish continuity inside the same live lease.

blocking_design_errata.title: Completed journal state and final lease validation are ordered inconsistently
blocking_design_errata.evidence: The policy docket requires final target, sentinel, process, evidence, and deadline validation before the transaction completed-state. The Windows docket also says to perform a final exact 13 readback and sentinel/process/identity check after completed. The existing process-crash kernel treats completed as a terminal verified state.
blocking_design_errata.risk: If an after-completed check detects drift, the design does not define whether completed may transition to recovery_required, whether the lock and marker still exist, or whether rollback would overwrite unknown concurrent bytes. A terminal success receipt could already be stale.
blocking_design_errata.required_resolution: Define one exact state machine. All authority-bearing final checks and durable receipt inputs must pass while lock, marker, journal ownership, sentinels, parent handles, and lease remain held, immediately before the single terminal completed transition. A post-completed read is diagnostic only. If it detects drift, classify the canonical state unknown, retain evidence, forbid automatic overwrite or rollback of unknown bytes, and require a separate human incident decision; never rewrite a terminal completed journal as though the drift occurred inside the transaction.

blocking_design_errata.title: Windows process liveness requirement uses incorrect signaling semantics and lacks an access-uncertainty stop
blocking_design_errata.evidence: The Windows docket requires process handles to remain signaled-as-running. On Windows, a process handle is normally nonsignaled while running and becomes signaled on exit. The design also does not explicitly state the outcome when a bounded process or executable identity cannot be opened because it exits, access is denied, or identity collection is incomplete.
blocking_design_errata.risk: An implementation could invert the liveness test or silently omit an unmeasurable writer row.
blocking_design_errata.required_resolution: Specify liveness mechanically, such as WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0) equals WAIT_TIMEOUT plus unchanged PID/start identity. Any access denied, process exit during capture, partial enumeration, missing executable handle identity, ambiguous PID reuse, protected bounded row, or unclassified executable is a hard block or coverage_unavailable in tests, never PASS.

blocking_design_errata.title: Hardlink admission policy is not closed
blocking_design_errata.evidence: The Windows docket rejects an alternate hardlink unless exact identity and a frozen link policy permit it, while the pure policy language generally lists hard-link alias as a fail-closed condition. The static allowlist has no link-count or hardlink policy field.
blocking_design_errata.risk: An unseen hardlink outside the governed parent can provide another name for mutating the same file object and weaken the exact parent-plus-leaf boundary.
blocking_design_errata.required_resolution: Select one rule. The recommended rule for this one-shot canonical operation is require a supported NTFS link-count observation equal to one for every target and sentinel at freeze, prepare, each pre-replacement check, publish, and final validation; any extra or unmeasurable link is a hard block. If exceptions are intended, enumerate exact allowed links and identities in the execution freeze and red-team them.

blocking_design_errata.title: Zero-delta test acceptance conflicts with the synthetic rooted-replacement case unless effect classes are scoped
blocking_design_errata.evidence: The V3 contract's real-Windows test gate requires exact zero governed-byte and directory-member delta, while WIN-V3-004 intentionally changes a target fixture to staged bytes and WIN-V3-005 exercises a replacement race.
blocking_design_errata.risk: A test receipt could either falsely claim zero bytes changed or mark the intended synthetic transaction as a failure, inviting selective interpretation.
blocking_design_errata.required_resolution: Split receipts. Read-only collector cases must prove zero target/sentinel byte and member delta, with metadata effects separately reported. Synthetic transaction cases must use a disposable fixture, list the exact intended byte transitions, prove zero out-of-scope changes, and either restore the fixture under a separately verified rollback or record its deliberate terminal test state before bounded cleanup. Neither receipt may be described as canonical execution.

blocking_design_errata.title: Static versus prepare-instance review scheduling is not defined within the 120-second same-process lease
blocking_design_errata.evidence: The prepare bundle binds checker and boss hashes, publish requires the same live lease and an unexpired owner capability, and all collection plus validation ages are capped at 120 seconds. The documents do not distinguish pre-restart static implementation reviews from any post-prepare instance review or say how an independent process could review live prepare evidence without breaking process/lease continuity.
blocking_design_errata.risk: A later workflow may demand a human or independent-agent review after prepare that cannot complete inside the lease, or may quietly reuse a static code review as if it reviewed the live prepare instance.
blocking_design_errata.required_resolution: Define review classes and timing. All implementation, test, contract, kernel, primitive, wrapper, and design reviews must be frozen before restart. Any live-instance check required before publication must be deterministic, bounded, read-only, and callable without transferring or reconstructing the lease; its exact function and expected digest must be pre-frozen. No human or asynchronous agent wait may occur inside the 120-second lease. If a required check cannot finish before expiry, stop without publication and discard the lease.

blocking_design_errata.title: The required non-model-forgeable owner capability does not currently exist
blocking_design_errata.evidence: The design resolution explicitly records that repository code has no established mechanism for a genuinely non-model-forgeable one-shot owner capability.
blocking_design_errata.risk: Implementation work may be mistaken for canonical readiness and local JSON, CLI text, an environment variable, or model-authored evidence may be substituted for the missing trust boundary.
blocking_design_errata.required_resolution: Add an explicit permanent stop condition: no canonical execution freeze, live canonical measurement, restart request, OneDrive action, prepare, publish, or recovery may be called ready until a specific product/runtime capability API exists, is outside model-controlled storage and inputs, is independently reviewed, and can enforce scope, expiry, revocation, one use, and exact digest bindings. Local fallbacks are forbidden.

required_stop_condition_additions: Stop if the detached-digest artifact graph has any direct or transitive hash cycle or lacks a named external trust anchor.
Stop if any pre-restart freeze contains an ephemeral PID, process start token, live handle, lease nonce, or live ancestry expectation.
Stop if a post-completed mismatch is treated as ordinary rollback authority or if unknown concurrent bytes may be overwritten.
Stop if any bounded process row is inaccessible, exits during observation, lacks an executable handle identity, is ambiguously reused, or cannot be classified exactly.
Stop if any target or sentinel has an unapproved or unmeasurable NTFS hardlink count.
Stop if a read-only zero-delta receipt and a synthetic transaction-delta receipt are conflated.
Stop if any required live-instance review cannot complete deterministically inside the same lease before its monotonic deadline.
Stop until the external owner-capability mechanism exists and is independently verified; never substitute local JSON, CLI text, workspace files, environment variables, or model-authored tokens.
Stop if access-time or cloud hydration uncertainty is reported as zero filesystem effect.
Stop if a strict writer-race appeal is marked resolved by handle retention, bounded process inventory, or temporary-root tests.

appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.position: Closed canonical JSON plus exact digests should allow publication to resume in a later process.
appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.reason: Bytes do not retain handles, process identity, lease time, sentinels, or owner-capability consumption state.

appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.position: Pure policy should verify that Lowell personally authorized the action.
appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.reason: Policy may validate scope and digest projections only; identity and capability origin remain external.

appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.position: Exact current and parent process continuity makes the genuine Codex runtime impossible.
appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.reason: The direct ancestry exception is a plausible bounded design, but its executable identities, access rights, liveness, and lease continuity have not been implemented or exercised on the actual host.

appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.position: Compatible retained handles and bounded process closure eliminate the writer race.
appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.reason: They detect and narrow risk but cannot exclude every pre-opened, future, hidden, kernel, sync, ancestor-thread, or noncooperating writer under delete sharing.

appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.position: A code-fixed launcher constant is the simplest trusted execution-freeze digest source.
appeal_and_disagreement_rulings.reason: It is invalid if the execution freeze or component lock contains the launcher hash. The trust anchor must be detached and outside the object graph it authenticates.

preserved_strict_writer_race_dissent.reason: Even a correct V3 implementation cannot prove exclusion of the precheck-to-rename lost-update window or post-readback-to-completed overwrite window while replacement requires delete sharing. The allowed Codex or shell ancestor itself also remains a possible writer.
preserved_strict_writer_race_dissent.human_question: Only after the corrected V3 design, implementation, deterministic negatives, real-Windows temporary-root tests, independent checker, premortem, boss review, and external owner-capability gate are all green: should Lowell require offline deterministic writer exclusion, or knowingly accept the exact residual lost-update and stale-completion races for one candidate-only 13-target Hosea publication?

honest_reuse_ruling.required_treatment: Preserve the five reviewed design inputs and this ruling append-only. Issue a corrected immutable design resolution that binds these errata and the same appeals. Then obtain a fresh design consistency check before implementation. No prior design PASS may be inferred.

next_action: Preserve this HOLD append-only. Correct the V3 design boundary for the eight blocking errata, especially the acyclic trust graph, stable-versus-ephemeral identity split, terminal completed-state ordering, Windows liveness semantics, hardlink policy, test-delta scopes, review timing, and missing external owner capability. Obtain a fresh independent design consistency review before implementing any V3 component. Do not perform live canonical measurement, restart, OneDrive action, prepare, publish, recover, canonical/global mutation, or publication from these design documents.
